subtitle: Out Manila · Cebu Pacific
overview: A winter route across central Japan: Takayama Old Town and Jinya, the thatched-roof village of Shirakawa-go, a sled stop at Takanbo Ski Resort, Kanazawa’s Kenrokuen Garden and Higashi Chaya District, then Osaka Castle, Fushimi Inari, Arashiyama and Nara Park. Fly Manila – Nagoya and return from Osaka with Cebu Pacific; stay in 3.5–4-star hotels.
travelDatesNote: Departures from Manila, Feb 20–24 2027 to Feb 20–24 2027. The rate changes by date: an amount on a date is added to the base rate per pax. Seats are limited and confirmed at booking.

placeDesc.Nagoya: A major city in central Japan where the tour lands at Chubu airport and spends the first night.
placeDesc.Takayama Jinya: The former government office of the Edo-period Takayama region, preserved as a historic building.
placeDesc.Takayama Old Town: A well-preserved old merchant district of wooden houses, sake breweries and shops in the Hida region.
placeDesc.Shirakawa-go: A UNESCO World Heritage village of steep thatched gassho-style farmhouses in the mountains.
placeDesc.Takanbo Ski Resort: A ski resort where the tour includes a snow sled ride, depending on natural snowfall.
placeDesc.Kenrokuen Garden: One of Japan's most celebrated landscape gardens, in Kanazawa.
placeDesc.Higashi Chaya District: A preserved geisha teahouse district in Kanazawa with traditional wooden facades.
placeDesc.Osaka Castle: A landmark 16th-century castle in Osaka, visited as a photo stop.
placeDesc.Arashiyama Bamboo Grove: A path through tall bamboo in western Kyoto.
placeDesc.Fushimi Inari Taisha: A Kyoto shrine famous for thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up a hill.
placeDesc.Nara Park: A large park in Nara where friendly deer roam freely near historic temples.
placeDesc.Rinku Premium Outlets: An outlet shopping centre near Kansai airport, about a 10-minute walk from the Day 4 hotel.
